cards.text: Moses is still preaching to Israel, laying out how God's people are supposed to live. He starts this part with who they are: sons of the LORD their God. Then he gives them a rule for when someone dies.

cards.question: When someone dies, what does Moses say Israel must not do for the dead?

answers.text: Cut themselves or shave their foreheads
Tear their clothes and wear sackcloth
Mourn for more than seven days

cards.question: Why does Moses say Israel must not cut themselves for the dead?

answers.text: They are a people holy to the LORD
Only the priests may mourn like that
The land they live in isn't theirs yet

cards.question: Moses says the LORD chose Israel to be His prized possession out of all the peoples on the face of the earth.

cards.text: Then Moses walks right into the kitchen, and friend, I LIVE in a kitchen, so I'm leaning WAY in. First rule: they must not eat any detestable thing.
Then he lists the animals they may eat: the ox, the sheep and the goat, plus wild ones like the deer, the gazelle, the ibex and the mountain sheep.

cards.question: Moses gives Israel a simple test for land animals they may eat. What two things must the animal have?

answers.text: A split hoof and it chews the cud
Horns and a thick woolly coat
Four legs and a short tail

cards.text: Then Moses names some animals that chew the cud: the camel, the rabbit and the rock badger.

cards.question: Because the camel, the rabbit and the rock badger chew the cud, Israel may eat them.

cards.text: Then comes the pig. It's got the divided hoof, so it's halfway there, which is exactly how my stamps came out my last year on the Millers' counter.

cards.question: The pig has a divided hoof. So why is it unclean for Israel?

answers.text: It does not chew the cud
It rolls around in the mud

cards.question: Israel must not eat the pig's meat, and they must not touch its carcass either.

cards.text: Now Moses heads into the water. Everything that swims gets one test too.

cards.question: For Israel to eat a creature that lives in the water, it needs ___ and ___.

cards.text: Then the birds. Any clean bird is fine, but Moses lists the ones that aren't, from the eagle and the raven to every kind of owl, and at the very end, the bat.

cards.question: Moses says flying insects are clean for Israel to eat.

cards.text: After the birds, Moses gets to any carcass. Israel can't eat it, but he doesn't tell them to throw it out.

cards.question: A carcass Israel can't eat may be given or sold to a ___.

cards.text: Moses reminds them again that they're a holy people belonging to the LORD. Then one last kitchen rule: they must not cook a young goat in its mother's milk.
Now Moses moves from the plate to the field. Every year, Israel must set aside part of what their fields bring in.

cards.question: Each year, Israel must set aside a ___ of all the produce from their fields.

cards.text: That tenth covers grain, new wine and oil, plus the firstborn of their herds and flocks. And Moses says what to do with it.

cards.question: What does Moses tell Israel to do with that tenth of their grain, wine, oil and firstborn animals?
Moses says eating the tithe before the LORD will teach Israel something. What is it?

answers.text: To fear the LORD their God always
To remember their years in the desert
To work their fields a little harder

cards.text: They're to eat it at the place the LORD will choose as a dwelling for His Name, but some of them will live too far away to carry it all. Friend, I can barely carry ONE cookie box, and I've got a mustache built for it.

cards.question: If the trip is too far, Moses says they can exchange the tithe for money and take the money with them.

cards.text: So they show up at the place the LORD chose, money in hand. Now Moses tells them how to spend it.

cards.question: Moses says the tithe money can only be spent on cattle and sheep.
Moses says they are to feast in the presence of the LORD and ___ with their household.

cards.text: Hold on. HOLD ON. The tithe ends in a FEAST? Friend, I've seen office parties with half that much joy.
But in all that celebrating, Moses tells them not to neglect the Levite living in their towns.

cards.question: Why does Moses say Israel must not neglect the Levite?

answers.text: He has no portion or inheritance
He is too old to farm the land
He guards the gates of the city

cards.text: Then Moses adds something that happens at the end of every three years.

cards.question: At the end of every three years, where does Israel lay up that year's tenth?
Along with the Levite, who may come and eat from that third-year tithe until they're satisfied?

answers.text: The foreigner and fatherless and widow
The priests and elders and judges
The soldiers and the king's servants

cards.question: Moses says that when they share the tithe this way, the LORD will bless them in all the work of their hands.

cards.text: And that's where we'll set the timer for now. Moses is still preaching, friend, and he's nowhere near his last point.

findings.problem: The question asks what two things the animal must 'have'. The right answer 'A split hoof and it chews the cud' is a noun plus a clause and reads awkwardly after 'have'. The wrong answers are both plain noun pairs ('Horns and a thick woolly coat', 'Four legs and a short tail'). The right answer is also the only one that sounds like the Bible ('chews the cud'), so it stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The card says Moses lists 'every kind of owl.' Deuteronomy 14:15-17 names specific owls (the screech owl, little owl, great owl, white owl and desert owl). Only the kite, raven, hawk and heron get 'any kind of.' 'Every kind of owl' stretches the text.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The card cites Deuteronomy 14:20-21 but tells only 14:21, the carcass rule. 'After the birds' doesn't tell 14:20 ('But you may eat any clean bird'), so the citation is too wide. It should be Deuteronomy 14:21.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card says 'That tenth covers grain, new wine and oil, plus the firstborn of their herds and flocks.' In 14:23, the tenth is of the grain, new wine and oil. The firstborn are listed separately and are not a tenth. The card makes the firstborn part of the tithe, which the text shows is not right.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The question says 'that tenth of their grain, wine, oil and firstborn animals,' which calls the firstborn animals a tenth. Deuteronomy 14:23 separates the tenth of grain, new wine and oil from the firstborn of the herds and flocks.

rule.text: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'Store it in a barn' is close to 14:28, where the third-year tenth is laid up within their gates. A baker could argue that storing the tithe is something the passage tells them to do.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The card says 'some of them will live too far away to carry it all.' Deuteronomy 14:24 is a condition: 'But if the distance is too great for you to carry...'. The card turns the 'if' into a statement that it will happen.

The card tells nothing new. The feast was already told in the card 10 question ('feast in the presence of the LORD'). Card 11 only reacts to the feast and recaps it, without moving the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The statement says 'when they share the tithe this way, the LORD will bless them,' which makes the blessing depend on the sharing. The BSB of 14:29 joins the two with only 'And the LORD your God will bless you in all the work of your hands.' The card adds a connection the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
